BiblicalUsage: He becometh poor that dealeth with a slack hand, but the hand of the diligent maketh rich, and the hand of the diligent shall bear rule while the slothful is under tribute. Blessed is the man unto whom the LORD imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile, and Micah charges the city whose rich men are full of violence and whose inhabitants speak lies with a deceitful tongue.
TheologicalSignificance: What I take from this is that deceit and slackness are the same sin wearing two faces. The slack hand will not do the work, and the deceitful tongue will not tell the truth, and both rob a man in the end. Blessed is the man with no guile in his spirit, because the LORD counts that honesty as righteousness.
